info.title: Chronary API
info.description:
Calendar-as-a-service API for AI agents.

Manage calendars, events, and availability for AI and human agents.
All endpoints require an API key passed as a Bearer token.

**Authentication:** `Authorization: Bearer chr_sk_...` or `Authorization: Bearer chr_ak_...`

**Rate limit:** 10 requests/second per API key on Free, 25 on Developer, 50 on Pro. Exceeds return HTTP 429.

**Quotas:** Monthly operation limits by plan — see [Billing & plans](https://docs.chronary.ai/resources/billing/) and [Rate limits](https://docs.chronary.ai/resources/rate-limits/).

**Agent bootstrap:** Custom extensions prefixed `x-agent-*` describe the self-signup flow for AI agents. These are not part of any registered OpenAPI extension — they are a Chronary convention.

Returns the catalog of publicly-available plans with pricing, limits, and display metadata. No authentication required; IP-rate-limited. Responses are cacheable (`Cache-Control: public, max-age=300, s-maxage=3600, stale-while-revalidate=86400`) with an `ETag` for 304 conditional requests.

get.summary: Get current Terms of Service version
get.description: Returns the latest ToS manifest entry. No authentication required — intended for CLIs, SDKs, and agent-signup flows that need to read the current version at runtime rather than rely on a build-time constant.

patch.summary: Accept the current Terms of Service
patch.description: Appends an immutable row to `tos_acceptances` (source=`reaccept`) capturing the accepting org, client IP, user-agent, and the ToS document SHA-256, then updates the denormalized `accepted_terms_version` / `accepted_terms_at` columns on the organization. Authenticated via JWT (console session cookie or Bearer token), not an API key. Allowed while the organization is scheduled for deletion: it only records the acceptance and does not change the deletion date.

Reaches the same re-acceptance path (appends an immutable `tos_acceptances` row and updates the org). Requires an org-level API key (`chr_sk_*`) — agent-scoped keys are rejected with 403.

get.summary: Export all account data (GDPR Art. 15 + 20 portability)
get.description: Returns a JSON dump of every row this org owns: agents, calendars, events (with decrypted titles + descriptions), iCal subscriptions, webhook subscriptions, availability rules, scheduling proposals + slots + responses, API key prefixes, ToS acceptance history, usage/quota counters, feedback, upgrade requests, booking pages, the audit log, Human calendar Connections with their external calendars, availability grants, publication bindings and setup links, and webhook deliveries. Webhook secrets, iCal subscription URLs, iCal feed tokens and Human calendar provider identifiers are redacted unless `include_secrets=true` is passed from a session that signed in within the last 5 minutes. Human calendar provider credentials are never exported. Internal infrastructure data (incident_records, scheduling internals, password/OTP/key hashes, claim tokens) is excluded. JWT-authenticated (console session cookie or Bearer token). Rate-limited to 10 exports/hour/org. An export larger than the synchronous download limit returns `413 export_too_large`; contact support for the complete file. Response includes `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Content-Disposition: attachment` so the browser triggers a download.

After 24h a cron promotes the claim and transfers all org-scoped resources.

Requires a console session re-authenticated within the last 5 minutes (else 401 `reauth_required`). One pending change per organization: a new request replaces the previous link. Answers 202 whether or not the address already belongs to another account.

post.description:
Create an organization and restricted API key by submitting an email and the current terms-of-service version.

Three server-side dedup branches — all return HTTP 200 (or 409 only for stale ToS) to block email enumeration:

- **New email** → returns `org_id` + `api_key`. OTP sent to email.
- **Duplicate unverified-agent signup with current ToS** → opaque response (no `org_id`/`api_key`). OTP rotated and re-sent.
- **Duplicate verified / console-origin org** → opaque response. No email sent.
- **Stale `tos_version`** (agent-origin) → 409 with `current_version` hint.

While sign-ups are paused (waitlist mode or early access full), every address gets the same 202 `{ waitlisted: true, message }` with no key and no `org_id`, whether it is new, already waitlisted or has an account.

A new verification code for an unverified org is emailed at most once per 60 seconds, and at most 3 sign-up calls per hour and 10 per day are accepted for one address; past that the call returns the same opaque 200 and sends nothing. Wrong codes add up across re-sends: after 30, the code is burned and no new one is sent for 24 hours.

The returned key is bound to an *unverified* org. It is fully usable for reads and writes within the standard per-resource quotas, but the org cannot graduate from the introductory `free-agent-unverified` plan tier until you call `POST /v1/agent/verify` with the emailed OTP. Verification rotates the org to its normal plan (`free` or — during the soft-launch window — `pro` via the auto-grant capacity gate) when early access has room; otherwise the org keeps Sandbox limits until a spot opens (see `POST /v1/agent/verify`).

Rate limits: 5 requests per 60 seconds per client IP, plus a per-network sign-up budget (default 20 per UTC hour and 50 per UTC day per IPv4 address or IPv6 /64), plus 10 sign-ups per UTC hour per email domain (large consumer providers such as gmail.com and outlook.com are exempt). Over any limit returns 429 `rate_limit_error` with a `Retry-After` header.

Disposable (throwaway) email addresses are refused with 400 `disposable_email` (`param: "email"`). Use a permanent address.
post.x-agent-hint: Call this first. Returns a restricted API key that works immediately for reads + writes. Follow up with POST /v1/agent/verify once the human reads the OTP.

On success the org transitions `status: unverified → verified`.
